vault.title: Lab 01 - Image basics (numpy)
vault.summary: This document outlines the first laboratory assignment for an Introduction to Computer Vision course, focusing on treating images as NumPy arrays. Students are required to build a 64x64 RGB gradient image, convert it to grayscale, perform array slicing for cropping and flipping, compute intensity histograms, and apply thresholding to generate an ASCII art mask. The deliverable is a Jupyter notebook named lab01.ipynb containing code cells for each task, to be submitted on WSP.
key_terms: NumPy: A library for programming in Python that adds support for large, multi-dimensional arrays and matrices.
Grayscale: An image in which the value of each pixel is a single sample representing only amount of light.
Array Slicing: A feature in Python to extract a portion of an array using start, stop, and step parameters.
Histogram: An accurate graphical representation of the tonal distribution in a digital image.
Thresholding: A simplest method of image segmentation that isolates objects by converting grayscale images to binary images.

vault.title: CSCI3240 Introduction to Computer Vision Syllabus
vault.summary: This document outlines the 15-week schedule for CSCI3240 Introduction to Computer Vision taught by Abenova Saule. Students will learn about image processing, feature detection, CNNs, and object detection through lectures and weekly labs. The course grading consists of 30 percent for labs, 30 percent for the midterm, and 40 percent for the final project.
key_terms: Convolution: A mathematical operation used in image filtering
Edge detection: Identifying points in an image where image brightness changes sharply
SIFT: Scale-Invariant Feature Transform for detecting and describing local features
Homography: A transformation relating the coordinates of points in two images
RANSAC: RANdom SAmple Consensus algorithm for robust fitting of models
CNN: Convolutional Neural Network used for image classification and detection

vault.title: CSCI3240 Lecture 01: Introduction
vault.summary: This introductory lecture for CSCI3240 Introduction to Computer Vision covers the course overview, grading policy, and the basics of representing digital images as arrays defined by height, width, channels, and uint8 data type. Students are also introduced to essential Python libraries used throughout the course, including numpy, OpenCV, and matplotlib.
key_terms: Images as arrays: A digital image represented numerically by its height, width, and color channels.
dtype uint8: An 8-bit unsigned integer data type commonly used for pixel intensity values ranging from 0 to 255.
numpy: A Python library used for numerical computations and array manipulations.
OpenCV: A library of programming functions mainly aimed at real-time computer vision.
matplotlib: A plotting library for Python used for visualizing images and data.
